title: Bondage to Addiction
definition: Bondage to Addiction describes enslaving patterns where desire, habit, escape, and sin become ruling powers that require truth, grace, community, and Spirit-empowered change.
summary: Bondage to Addiction describes enslaving patterns where desire, habit, escape, and sin become ruling powers that require truth, grace, community, and Spirit-empowered change.
christFocus: Christ breaks the dominion of sin and gives His Spirit, His people, and His Word for a new way of life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Bondage to Addiction teaches that addiction reveals how sin can master the will, deform desire, and create chains that need both Gospel deliverance and patient discipleship. Scripture tells the truth about humanity without denying dignity and without minimizing the ruin sin has brought.

God gives this truth so people may stop hiding and come into the light. People in recovery need truth without condemnation and hope without denial. The Bible’s honesty is mercy because what remains hidden cannot be healed rightly.

Christ enters the truth this doctrine exposes. Christ breaks the dominion of sin and gives His Spirit, His people, and His Word for a new way of life. In Him, sinners are not left under guilt, shame, bondage, fear, or death; they are called to repentance, faith, restoration, and new life by the power of the Holy Spirit.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People need this truth because sin, shame, weakness, and brokenness are not solved by denial. People in recovery need truth without condemnation and hope without denial. Scripture tells the truth so that people may stop hiding and come to Christ.

It also protects believers from shallow answers. Humanity needs forgiveness, new birth, restoration, and Spirit-empowered obedience, not merely better circumstances or stronger willpower.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Walk in recovery as discipleship: honest confession, daily dependence, wise support, and Spirit-led obedience. Bring this doctrine into prayer, Scripture, and daily obedience. Ask the Holy Spirit to make the truth real in your thinking, desires, relationships, and next faithful step with Christ.
